stages.name: Exploitation of Exposed AI Control Points
observables: Outbound Burp Collaborator callbacks from RAGFlow server

stages.name: Gateway Runtime Secret Harvesting
observables: Python urllib, curl, or wget used for exfiltration of environment blocks

stages.name: Masqueraded Payload Delivery and Execution
observables: ELF binaries staged in temporary paths
Service-style naming masquerading as benign Linux daemons
Shell-stage downloaders with short timeouts and fallbacks

stages.name: Host Discovery and Competitor Cleanup
observables: Process sweeps for competing miners or remote shells
Modification of crontab to remove other miner entries

stages.name: AI Gateway Database Exfiltration
observables: Self-contained python3 one-liners installing PostgreSQL support

stages.name: Compute Resource Hijacking
observables: Loading Linux Model-Specific Register (msr) module with write access

stages.name: System Persistence and C2
observables: Modification of SSH authorized_keys under service accounts

scenario.summary: Attackers are targeting exposed AI infrastructure components like LiteLLM gateways, RAGFlow document engines, and Kestra orchestrators to harvest LLM provider keys and credentials. Once access is gained, they pivot to container host persistence and monetize compromised compute resources through cryptomining.

meta.rationale: The hunt should initially focus on hosts identified as running LiteLLM, RAGFlow, or Kestra using the software inventory step.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker has compromised an AI gateway or retrieval engine and is now deploying masqueraded payloads to monetize the host via cryptomining and establish durable SSH or systemd persistence.

blind_spots.risk: Legitimate system utilities might load the msr module; without seeing the write parameter, we cannot confirm if it was for mining tuning.
blind_spots.question: Was the msr module loaded with write access enabled (allow_writes=1)?

blind_spots.risk: Short-lived payloads might be missed if the data source relies on periodic process snapshots rather than an execution stream.
blind_spots.question: Did the payload execute and terminate between snapshots?

blind_spots.risk: We can see the file was touched but not what key was added, preventing attribution to a known actor without host forensics.
blind_spots.question: What public key was added to authorized_keys?

hunt.name: AI Infrastructure Host Monetization and Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt focuses on the post-exploitation phase of attacks targeting AI infrastructure like LiteLLM, RAGFlow, and Kestra. It examines the transition from initial gateway command execution to host-level abuse. We first identify hosts running AI software, then hunt for masqueraded binaries in temporary paths using a prevalence baseline to find rare items. We corroborate these with host discovery commands, cryptomining indicators such as MSR module loading, and persistence mechanisms like SSH authorized_keys modifications.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_uid, device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{ai_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{ai_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(vendor_name) || ',') > 0)
config.description: Scope the hunt to Linux hosts running targeted AI software or retrieval engines, retrieving both UIDs and hostnames for precise filtering.
config.expected_signal: A list of host UIDs and names currently running AI gateways or retrieval engines. This narrows the search for subsequent behavioural telemetry.

primitive_config.label: Identify AI infrastructure hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_uid, device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{ai_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{ai_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(vendor_name) || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: A list of host UIDs and names currently running AI gateways or retrieval engines. This narrows the search for subsequent behavioural telemetry.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS executions, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/var/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/dev/shm/%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING executions <= 10 AND hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Find masqueraded payloads by stack-counting binaries executed from world-writable directories.
config.expected_signal: Rare binaries executing from world-writable paths. Malicious binaries may run many times on a single victim but are rare across the fleet.

primitive_config.label: Rare binaries in temporary paths

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sudo -l%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%crontab -l%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%netstat -anp%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%rm %crontab%') AND (instr(',' || '{{ai_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(parent_process_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect commands used for environment fingerprinting launched directly from AI gateway parent processes.
config.expected_signal: A sequence of discovery commands or crontab modifications appearing on the same hosts that launched rare temporary binaries from the gateway context.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, module_name, process_name, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE LOWER(module_name) = 'msr' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
